lines.text: dying is something quite different from the implications of
death in man; it is not destruction, extinction, but the
transition to new forms of life. All growth and decay in
nature is swallowed up in a vast, unceasing stream of life.
In what sense then can it be said that nature stands under
the curse of transience?
And yet this thought contains a deep truth. Certainly,
nature, regarded in itself, does not seem to be burdened with
the curse of transience; but it does not exist for its own sake,
for the drama of man's history is enacted in its midst, and
whether it wills or no, it is drawn into the complex of that
drama, becomes involved in the fate of man, is violated and
despoiled by man. Do we not see this to-day, sometimes with
a feeling of horror?
It is difficult to say where this process of violation begins.
Perhaps already in the work of the tiller of the soil? In the
cultivation of garden and forest? This would not seem to be
the case. It is doubtful if Paul is thinking of this, for in such
dealings with nature man remains as it were in conformity
with the laws of nature's life; he tends its growth and reaps
its crops for the maintenance of his life and obviously is not
yet acting contrary to nature. For in so far as he needs
nourishment and seeks his nourishment in the realm of
nature, he is himself a being integral to nature, no other
than the animal, and with seed time and harvest his life is
merged in the great process of nature's vitalities.
But where does the violation of nature begin? We do not
know at what point specifically Paul himself saw man's
forcible subjugation of nature. He might have been thinking
of all kinds of phenomena of his time; but he gives us no
precise details. But there is no need to ponder the matter. The
fact of man's violation of nature is plain, and it is plainest
where human life has become most removed from the sphere
of nature, in big cities and wherever technics have gained an
all-controlling ascendancy. The very longing of the city
dweller to take refuge in nature from time to time is an
indication that in his normal environment nature has been
driven out, or trampled on and killed.
